scope: Retained one-MI50 F32-tile control versus native-F16-tile candidate development screen only; not an acceptance/performance qualification.

configuration.dtype: f16 requested; control reaches F32 NVFP4 tile while candidate uses native F16 tile (verified by actual path witnesses)
configuration.order: For each P: control warmup, candidate warmup, then measured control/candidate/candidate/control (ABBA). After all 12 timing calls, one separate P128/G1/r1 --profile path witness per arm.
configuration.clock_policy: default; no power or clock changes

monitoring.coverage_limitations: Short-lived processes between samples may be missed; disappeared/new and inaccessible processes are retained as coverage limits. Unavailable GPU counters are not zero.

prompt_equivalence_proof.llmx_source: src/cli/main.cpp bench_ids(seed,n,n_vocab), called with seeds 12345 for prompt and 777 for decode
prompt_equivalence_proof.statement: Patch uses same uint32 LCG and vocab mapping as llmx, resets matching seeds for each prompt and decode; llmx and mx use same pinned model bytes.

limitations: One short development screen; only two measured samples per arm per cell. Means are descriptive and no performance floor/qualification is claimed.
Control and candidate use different NVFP4 activation paths, so this is not an output-identity comparison.
MI50 MX precision comparison remains separate and pending; this screen compares two llmx builds only.
Monitor records full process/GPU/disk observations. GPU/process counters can be unknown; disk activity is aggregate and not attributable per process.
No full HF, depth, split, existing-format, current-head CI or merge gate is established by this screen.

retained_preflight_attempts.failure: Privileged Portainer mistaken for a GPU workload. Fixed only for the exact verified management container/image/command, with fuser empty required.
Docker emits lowercase no such object. Corrected case-insensitive diagnostic check.

kernel_diagnostic.scope: Separate P128/G1 profiled calls, not timing samples. No spills observed; instruction counts do not alone prove a bottleneck.
